name: LCF
note: Stanford theorem prover for Scott's Logic for Computable Functions; Edinburgh LCF later introduced ML
typeSystem: Simply typed logic of computable functions (Dana Scott's PCF-style domain theory); the Edinburgh LCF re-implementation added a small, strongly typed metalanguage, ML, purely so that proof-producing tactics could be type-checked before running.
runtime: Edinburgh LCF ran its ML metalanguage as an interpreter driving a proof-checking kernel; every LCF theorem had to be produced by composing a fixed, small set of trusted primitive inference rules. Its abstract-theorem architecture directly influenced HOL and Isabelle, while other proof assistants such as Coq likewise rely on a small trusted kernel.

runtimes.name: ML interpreter (Edinburgh LCF)
runtimes.role: Interprets the original ML metalanguage, executing tactics that manipulate the LCF proof kernel.

compilers.name: Edinburgh LCF implementation
compilers.role: Proof-checking environment consisting of the trusted kernel and ML tactic interpreter; it was not a compiler, but was a direct ancestor of Standard ML and HOL-family provers.

codeExample.caption: Conceptual tactic outline (schematic pseudocode, not literal historical LCF input)
codeExample.source:
FACT_POS_TAC :=
  INDUCTION
  THEN REWRITE USING factorial_definition
  THEN DISCHARGE arithmetic_subgoals

PROVE "for every n, factorial(n) is positive"
  USING FACT_POS_TAC
